newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian bullion closes down on weak global trends.
newsitem.headline: Indian bullion closes down on weak global trends.

text.p: ** Gold 24 carat closed 40 rupees lower at 4,730 rupees per 10 grammes, down against the previous close of 4,770 rupees on the back of fresh selling by stockists following the weak trend in the world market.
** Prices of a gold biscuit (116.50 gramme) closed 500 rupees lower at 55,300 rupees per piece. They were down by 200 rupees per piece on Monday.
** Silver (.999) closed 50 rupees lower at 7,305 rupees per kg against the previous close of 7,355 rupees amid sluggish industrial demand while a setback in the world market dragged prices lower.

Gold 24 carat closed 40 rupees lower at 4,730 rupees per 10 grammes against the previous close of 4,770 rupees on the back of sluggish seasonal buying while a weak trend in the world market prompted fresh unloading by stockists, dealers said.
Gold was down by 25 rupees per 10 grammes on Monday.
Gold biscuit prices (116.50 grammes) closed 500 rupees lower at 55,300 rupees each against the previous close of 55,800 rupees. They were down by 200 rupees each on Monday.
Sentiment at the close still remained subdued for gold amid slow physical enquiries but some traders expected gold prices to bounce back on Wednesday.
"The market is oversold at this juncture and may look up again," one broker said.

Silver (.999) closed 50 rupees lower at 7,305 rupees per kg against the previous close of 7,355 rupees on the back of continued arrivals of imported silver while industrial buyers kept to the sidelines expecting further price erosion in the falling market.
Silver was down 70 rupees per kg on Monday and 50 rupees last week. Sentiment for silver remained subdued at the close amid reports of a slide in the world market.
